prompt: A circle has radius $5$. What is the length of an arc that subtends a central angle of $1.2$ radians?
hint: When the angle is in radians, arc length has a very short formula.

hints.text: When the angle is in radians, arc length has a very short formula.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try radius $1$: an angle of $2$ radians subtends an arc of $2$, since $s = r\theta = 1 \times 2$. That is the definition of a radian, which is why the formula is so short.

explanation: For an angle measured in radians, arc length is $s = r\theta$ — no fractions of $360$ required.
This simplicity is the whole reason radians exist as a unit.

alternativeExplanations.title: The formula only works in radians
steps: With $\theta$ in degrees you must use $s = \dfrac{\theta}{360} \cdot 2\pi r$ instead.
Plugging a degree measure into $s = r\theta$ gives an answer far too large.
Check the units the question states before choosing the formula — the SAT mixes both deliberately.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Reaching for angle/360 × 2πr — the degree recipe — mangles a radian problem and produces a π that should not be there.
Radians earn the short formula: s = rθ = 5 × 1.2 = 6, no π anywhere. Check the angle's unit before choosing the recipe.
